note.note:
Consult Summary:
- 40-year-old female with ~3 weeks of left-sided facial numbness and reduced hearing, occasional tinnitus and intermittent dizziness.
- Clinician suspects possible Bell's palsy; urgent face-to-face neurological and ear examination arranged for today to confirm diagnosis and exclude other causes.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Left-sided facial numbness
- Onset/duration: Approximately 3 weeks.
- Description: Numbness localized to left side of face around left ear and along the left jawline; subjectively present at the time of consult.
- Associated symptoms: Occasional tinnitus; intermittent dizziness when tinnitus occurs.
- Systems review / pertinent negatives: No weakness elsewhere, no swallowing difficulty, no speech difficulty, no vision problems, no fever.
- Social/functional impact: Symptoms affecting work (reduced training and ability to perform jockey duties).
- Examination: No objective exam performed via video; numbness reported by patient.
- Differential / clinician impression: Clinician noted possible Bell's palsy but requires in-person neurological exam to confirm.

Issue 2: Left-sided hearing reduction and intermittent tinnitus
- Onset/duration: Concurrent with facial numbness (~3 weeks).
- Description: Decrease in hearing on the left side; intermittent ringing in the left ear.
- Associated symptoms: Occasionally associated dizziness.
- Systems review / pertinent negatives: No ear discharge, no ear pain, no itchiness reported.
- Examination: No otoscopic exam performed via video; clinician requested in-person ear inspection.

Issue 3: Nasal polyps (chronic) and remote labyrinthitis
- History: Patient reports prior diagnosis of nasal polyps; uses a prescribed nasal spray as needed (name not recalled). Patient reports remote history of labyrinthitis "ages ago" with no ongoing problems.
- Medications related: Nasal spray used when polyps flare (name not documented).
- Impact: Not currently reported as active issue contributing to present symptoms.

Medications:
- Rennies (antacid) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Nasal spray for nasal polyps — name not documented; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- No other regular medications reported.

Allergies:
- Latex.

Past Medical History:
- Nasal polyps.
- Remote history of labyrinthitis (patient recall; no ongoing symptoms reported).

Social History:
- Occupation: Jockey (horse racing); symptoms reducing ability to train/work.
- Living situation: Conflict noted — patient initially stated "I live alone" then stated "I live with my partner."
- Pets: None.
- Smoking/alcohol: Not mentioned.

Preventative History:
- No preventative care details (cervical screening, mammogram, PSA, FOBT, BMD, vaccinations, optometry, skin check) were mentioned.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not provided.
- Findings: No physical examination performed via video. Subjective findings recorded: persistent left-sided facial numbness; reduced left-sided hearing; occasional tinnitus; intermittent dizziness. No fever, no ear discharge, no ear pain reported. No focal limb weakness, no swallowing or speech difficulties, no vision disturbance reported.

Plan:
- Arrange same-day face-to-face clinic appointment for in-person neurological examination and otoscopic ear inspection to assess for Bell's palsy versus other causes.
- Clinician will message admin to book patient into a clinic slot; patient advised to call the support team number (to be left in notes) after five minutes to be slotted into a convenient appointment.
- Patient instructed to ensure the appointment occurs today for definitive assessment and reassurance.
- Further management and treatment to be determined after in-person assessment (no medications prescribed during this consult).

document_quality / Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: vital signs (BP, HR, temperature), formal neurological exam findings, otoscopic examination findings, medication doses/routes/frequencies, full medication reconciliation, name and dose of nasal spray.
- Internal conflicts from transcript: Patient's living situation conflicted — stated both "I live alone" and "I live with my partner."
- Transcript quality: Mostly clear; some brief inaudible words and minor conversational fillers but adequate to extract clinical information.
